L01.note: 125/133/149/157 are two pairs symmetric about a missing 141; no option is marked out.

L02.note: 120 = 6*20 and 26 = 6+20, so those two are derived traps; 20 is the larger primitive.

L03.note: 25, 5 and 12.5 are reachable by one step (5*5, given, half of 25); 7.5 is the only value needing real work.

L04.note: 180 / 225 / 281.25 is a x1.25 chain centred on 225, the hub the others are built from.

L05.note: 190/200/210 cluster with 130 far off; picked the round centre of the cluster.

L06.note: 45, 120, 180 are all round angle values; 72 is the only computed-looking one.

L07.note: 2.04 and 2.28 are a tight pair against 0.78 and 6.36; no reliable relation among them.

L08.note: 1, 9, 10 interlock (1+9=10) and 5 is the loner, but which side holds the key is undecidable.

L09.note: 20, 30, 38 are even/round; 23 is the only value that looks computed rather than chosen.

L11.note: 29 is the outlier; picked inside the 12-19 cluster with no further basis.

L12.note: 10, 15, 21 are consecutive triangular numbers, so the key sits in that family; 15 is its centre.

L13.note: 21/4 = 5.25 exactly, the classic shape where the two inputs are offered as distractors.

L15.note: 260 = 400 - 140, i.e. the completed difference while 400 and 140 are partial results; 4 is unit-error scale.

L17.note: all four are primes; 61/67/71 cluster tightly and 83 is the lone outlier.

L18.note: 414 and 427 are a near pair; nothing separates 583 from 648.

L19.note: 4/5 and -4/5 form a sign pair, which normally brackets the key; took the positive member.

L20.note: 31 is the outlier, 14/16/19 the cluster; picked within it arbitrarily.

L21.note: 3, 4, 5, 6 consecutive - the option set alone cannot decide this.

L22.note: 24, 15 and 40 are each a simple fraction of 60 (2/5, 1/4, 2/3), making 60 the hub.

L23.note: 5/-5 is a sign pair and 9 = 3^2 a squaring trap; took the positive member of the sign pair.

L24.note: 480 = 210+270 and 60 = 270-210, so both are derived traps; picked the larger primitive.

L25.note: 23 is the outlier against 4/7/9; no basis inside the cluster.

L26.note: 20 -> 30 -> 45 is a x1.5 chain, so 30 is the central value both others derive from.

L27.note: 65/73/85/93 are two pairs symmetric about 79, the same key-plus-offset shape as L01.

L28.note: 2, 3, 4 consecutive with -1 as a sign trap; nothing picks among the three.
